input: Set up a small home aquarium

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Freshwater vs. saltwater fundamentally changes equipment, cost, complexity, and maintenance — the entire plan differs depending on this choice.
Budget determines which tank size, filtration systems, lighting, and livestock are realistic options — a $100 budget vs. a $500 budget yields very different setups.
The intended room or location affects tank size (space available), lighting needs (natural light exposure), and surface/structural considerations.
Knowing the experience level of the person setting it up (complete beginner vs. returning hobbyist) shapes how much guidance, equipment simplicity, and hand-holding the plan needs.
The desired fish or aquatic life (e.g., community fish, a betta, live plants, invertebrates) drives stocking, tank size, water parameters, and decor choices.
Whether the user plans to buy equipment online vs. locally, and how soon they want the tank running, affects the sequencing and timeline of the plan.
Understanding what 'done well' means to the user — a fully cycled, stocked tank vs. just having the hardware set up — determines where the plan ends and how success is measured.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a small home aquarium
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to plan and execute the setup of a small aquarium in their home, from selecting equipment to having a functioning tank.

questions.title: Freshwater, saltwater, or brackish tank?
questions.description: Which type of aquarium does the user want to set up? This is the single most consequential decision, as it determines equipment, cost, and complexity across the entire project.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this setup?
questions.description: Understanding the available budget shapes every purchasing decision, from the tank and filter to livestock and decor.

questions.title: Which room or spot will the tank live in?
questions.description: The intended location determines the maximum tank footprint, proximity to power outlets, sunlight exposure, and whether the surface can support the weight.

questions.title: How much aquarium experience do you have?
questions.description: A complete beginner needs a simpler, more guided plan with forgiving equipment, while a returning hobbyist can handle more complexity.

questions.title: What fish or aquatic life do you want to keep?
questions.description: The desired inhabitants drive tank size minimums, water chemistry targets, compatibility planning, and decor or plant requirements.

questions.title: Will you shop locally, online, or both?
questions.description: The sourcing approach affects how tasks are sequenced, lead times for equipment arrival, and whether livestock can be sourced immediately.

questions.title: What does a successful setup look like to you?
questions.description: Clarifying the end goal — hardware installed, tank fully cycled, or fish happily living in the tank — defines where the plan ends and what milestones matter most.
